1.0 Introduction 
The Research Incubation (RI) program at Vijaybhoomi University aims to equip students with 
critical thinking and problem-solving skills. This program will facilitate students to develop 
research-oriented thinking which will enable them to thrive and innovate in today’s fast-changing 
business and technical environment. 
This Research Incubation program applies only to UG Programs and is offered in every term. For 
a 3-year UG program, students can register for an RI course after completing one and a half years 
and 60 credits. For the 4 and 5-year UG program, students need to register for RI after completing 
two years and 80 credits. 
In order to better facilitate the academic and aspirational diversity of our students, RI offers three 
tracks as follows 
• Research Track 
• Innovation Track (To be offered in the future, with separate guidelines) 
• Incubation Track (To be offered in the future, with separate guidelines) 
Each track will have its own set of requirements and passing criteria. Every student must select 
one of the above 3 tracks to complete their RI requirements. Guidelines for each track will be 
issued on the required basis, which will be explained every time during the RI workshop and RI 
course registration. 
There will be an RI Governance Council which will consist of representatives from all schools 
called Research Coordinators, who will be overall responsible for the RI activities from all the 
schools.

2.0 Research Track 
The purpose of this track is to enable students with an advanced interest and skill set in research 
to dig deeper into a particular problem and get “real-world” experience in conducting research. 
The RI course assessments are aligned with the General Learning Goals that aim to achieve the 
University’s mission of nurturing holistic, socially responsible, and continuously employable 
individuals. 
By the end of the RI course, students will be able to read research papers independently, conduct 
a literature review, identify research gaps, collect primary/secondary data, perform data analysis, 
and interpret results from the data analysis. Students will be expected to communicate at least one 
original research paper to a peer-reviewed research journal (with Scopus indexing/Web of Science 
indexing) or file an original patent based on their research work. 
2.1 Objective of Research Track 
1. To encourage the students to develop the knowledge, attitudes, and skills to be lifelong, 
self-directed learners. 
2. To help students acquire the knowledge and skills to complete the components of a 
research project including: 
a) Identification of a challenging problem or an area of research. 
b) Teamwork. 
c) Participation in data collection, analysis, and interpretation. 
d) Application of appropriate methods to arrive at and interpret the results. 
e) Oral dissemination of research information. 
f) Written dissemination of research information. 
3. To train students to evaluate the relative effectiveness of alternative solutions for 
addressing the problem(s).

2.2 Process Flow of Research Incubation 
Step I: Coursework 
• Students must have completed all GE credits as a prerequisite before starting the RI. 
• Students must have completed the SIP course as a prerequisite before starting the RI. 
• Students must attend the “Research Methodology” workshop conducted during the 
first week of course registration. Attending the RI workshop is compulsory. Marks 
will be allocated based on the performance of the students in a test conducted after 
the workshop. 
• Faculties (RI mentors) should assign courses in Coursera related to the research topic, 
which must be completed by students within two terms of registration. 
Step II: Research Cluster 
The Research Cluster is formed based on the convergence of interest between the faculty 
and students. The Research cluster/group consists minimum of 2 and a maximum of 4 
students from the same school and is assigned to a faculty mentor. However, one faculty 
mentor can handle only one group. Students should choose faculty from the same school, 
and the research topics should be relevant to their course. 
Step III: Identification of Research Area 
The Research Incubation Program will start with the faculty members submitting their 
research proposals in their area of interest, which will be circulated to all the students by 
the respective school RI coordinators. Students along with RI faculty mentors will discuss 
and finalize the Research Proposal. 
Step IV: Research Framework & Methodology 
Once the research problem is identified, the problem will be validated by the research 
committee, to ensure whether the research problem has already been addressed, or not. To 
attain this objective, a review of the relevant literature must be carried out. Based on the 
studies done in the past and the results of those studies, one can know, whether the present 
research problem has already been addressed or not. Literature review broadens the scope 
of the research problem, i.e., if the researcher follows the top-down approach, then first

Step V: Credits and Course Duration

2.3 Research Progression 
2.3.1 Assessment 
Specific slots for Research Incubation will be scheduled in the Timetable of the faculty and 
students post the initial Introduction to Research classroom sessions. The RI slot will be 
for a minimum of two hours per week per research cluster, which can be both 
supervised/unsupervised/blend of both and is meant for the faculty to guide and mentor 
their respective students. Faculty mentors will do a weekly review of the students’ 
timetables, and the progress of the student is assessed as per Annexure I. This will also 
serve as a time sheet for the continuous evaluation and the grading of each student and 
must be maintained in LMS. The faculty mentor and Research coordinators should

The students will have research progress presentations every month before the faculty 
mentor and the research committee. The research progress presentation evaluation form is 
shown in Annexure II. Evaluation of the final presentation will be done by the RI Faculty 
mentor and RI Coordinators. The final RI presentation evaluation is shown in Annexure 
III. 
RI coordinators will issue a course diary, which is mandatory to maintain in the physical 
form throughout the course completion. RI dairy would have all the course discussions 
and weekly sessions details with weekly, monthly, and milestone progress details and 
assessment records. In case faculties or students are maintaining the course diary online, 
they should notify the RI coordinator of this deviation and get prior approval. 
The students need to complete their research paper before the start of their final Internships. 
Each Research Cluster will submit its draft paper/progress at the end of each term to the 
Research Committee for tracking. The Research Committee will do a separate evaluation 
of the quality of the draft paper/progress, to track the progress of the Research Cluster. 
2.3.2 Final Review 
Every completed research paper should undergo an internal review process by the Research 
Committee before being communicated to the Journal (Scopus/Web of Science 
Indexing/UGC Care List 1). 
2.4 Marks 
The weightage of marks for Research Incubation will be distributed across the 5 mandatory 
submissions: Literature Review, Research Methodology & Data Collection, Data Analysis 
and Interpretation, first written report, and Final viva Voce. The final marks of each RI 
cluster will be determined by the Screening Committee depending on the content and 
publishing potential of the research paper. The student will get a separate certificate for the

3.0 Operational Framework of RI Tracks 
The Organizational Framework for the RI course is given below: 
• The Practice Courses Governance Council at Vijaybhoomi University will oversee the 
execution of the RI for the Undergraduate students at Vijaybhoomi University. 
• The Council will be led by the RI Chair and Co-chair. 
• The coordinators of each School will work closely with the RI Chair and Co-chair to 
ensure the delivery and execution of the RI course. 
RI Practice Courses Governance Council 
The RI committee will have the responsibility of ensuring that the RI course is delivered to all 
Undergraduate Students across various schools. 
The school RI coordinators will take care of the following steps: 
• One month before the start of every term, the school RI coordinator will ask the respective 
deans of each of the schools to provide the list of students who have completed their credits 
and all requirements for doing RI. 
• Each faculty member needs to submit their research topic(s) to their respective school RI 
coordinators during the time the RI course is offered. 
• Students at each school who are eligible for the RI course will choose the preferred RI topic 
and faculty only from their respective schools.

• Deans will ensure that the students who have opted for the RI course have completed all 
the Prerequisites. 
• With the approval of deans, the RI school coordinators will finalize the list of RI students 
from their respective schools. 
• Depending on the number of students at the respective schools that have chosen RI, the RI 
chair and co-chair will work with the respective school RI coordinators to ensure the 
following: 
a) Sufficient number of Research Proposals (in the correct format) are present and 
floated for those students who have opted for RI. 
b) For students who wish to convert their RI program to II, a psychometric test should 
be conducted. Post the psychometric test, the students need to present their ideas to 
a Jury Committee. In case the students’ ideas are not selected by the Jury 
Committee, the students are to be instructed to continue in the RI program. 
(Separate guidelines will be issued after considering individual cluster 
requirements). 
• The respective School RI coordinators will ensure that the mandatory weekly meetings 
between students and faculty are conducted. 
• The RI committee will ensure that the research proposals will be translated into publishable 
research papers. 
• It is compulsory for all the students to publish their research work in any of the following 
formats: Journal articles/Conference papers/Book chapters. 
• To get A+/A they have to publish in Scopus listed publications. 
• The RI committee will ensure that the Research or Conference papers that are produced as 
an outcome of the RI Track are communicated to the respective Journals/Conferences only 
via the faculty’s official email ID. 
• The RI chair and co-chair along with the respective school RI coordinators will ensure that 
all the timelines mentioned in the Handbook are adhered to, including the various progress 
reports and grading. 
• The school RI coordinators will highlight any deviations or delays in the process for the 
various tracks at their respective schools’ Faculty Council Meetings. This would help the 
RI committee to rectify any issues.
